{"content":"","tool_calls":[{"name":"Write","arguments":"{\"file_path\":\"/tmp/hint_output.md\",\"content\":\"# Auto TOC implementation guide\\n\\n## Problem Essence\\n\\nThe current repository has no Auto TOC rule or TOC-generation utility, so opting in with a marker cannot produce or update a contents list. The existing heading regex and rule framework provide useful pieces, but they do not themselves identify a TOC region, construct anchors, or prevent headings in ignored blocks from being collected.\\n\\n## Key Files and Locations\\n\\n- `src/rules/auto-toc.ts` (new): define and default-export the registered content rule, its option defaults, settings controls, examples, and the call into the TOC utility. Declare code, math, and YAML ignore types in the rule metadata.\\n- `src/utils/toc.ts` (new): isolate marker handling, heading extraction, text normalization, exclusions, anchor deduplication, and list generation from the UI-facing rule.\\n- `src/rules-runner.ts`: import the new rule so its registration decorator executes and the normal rule loop can discover it. The reference patch adds an import rather than a special execution path.\\n- `src/lang/locale/en.ts`: add the rule and option name/description keys and dropdown enum labels used by the builders.\\n- `src/rules/rule-builder.ts`: inspect `NumberOptionBuilder` and its generic key constraint. The reference changes its value type from `Number` to `any` to accommodate the new numeric options; consider the wider type-safety impact when making the change.\\n\\nSupporting code worth studying: `src/utils/regex.ts` defines `allHeadersRegex` and its capture groups; `src/utils/ignore-types.ts` implements placeholder-based ignore handling; `src/rules/remove-trailing-punctuation-in-heading.ts` and `src/rules/ordered-list-style.ts` show existing rule patterns.\\n\\n## Solution Approach\\n\\nConnect a conventional `RuleBuilder` rule to a focused utility. The framework constructs options and registers the rule, while the utility finds the first opt-in marker, collects eligible headings outside the selected TOC region, and replaces or inserts the generated content. Preserve the rest of the document and return it unchanged when there is no start marker.\\n\\nSeparate the heading's displayed text from its anchor: resolve links and remove embeds and formatting when creating the anchor, but only strip displayed formatting when the corresponding option requests it. Apply exclusions before rendering, maintain a document-order counter for duplicate bases, and render indentation and list markers from the options.\\n\\n## Implementation Directions\\n\\n1. Follow a nearby registered rule to implement the class, `OptionsClass`, examples, and option builders. Provide the defaults in the issue; ensure dropdown values have matching English locale keys. Trace how `buildRuleOptions` converts configuration keys into properties, including the newline-separated textarea. Numeric settings are presented through a text option, so account for conversion at the rule boundary.\\n2. In the utility, locate markers case-insensitively with whitespace tolerance. Match the first end marker *after* the first start, and distinguish an existing region from a missing end marker. Rebuild the region with the requested blank-line boundaries, preserving surrounding content and ensuring a second run is stable.\\n3. Inspect `allHeadersRegex`: its second capture is the hash sequence and its fourth is the heading text; it also has a separate optional closing-hash capture. Filter heading levels to the configured range and exclude positions in the selected TOC region. Use the rule's ignore mechanism for YAML, code, and math, and verify the actual rule execution path as well as direct calls to the utility.\\n4. Normalize heading text in a deliberate order: remove wiki and Markdown image embeds before resolving ordinary links to display text, remove formatting and trailing heading hashes, then lowercase, replace whitespace, filter characters, collapse hyphens, and trim them. Handle a trailing explicit ID separately when enabled. Track repeated anchor bases while processing headings in order.\\n5. Compare exclusions case-insensitively, distinguishing slash-delimited regular expressions from literal entries. Render the optional title and each surviving heading with the requested marker, indentation relative to `minLevel`, and either constant or globally incrementing ordered numbers.\\n6. Add focused tests using the repository's existing rule-test conventions. Cover the rule through its framework entry point as well as any utility-level behavior; check expected output and idempotence rather than only whether an entry exists.\\n\\n## Pitfalls and Edge Cases\\n\\n- Test no marker, mixed case and tabs in markers, an end marker before the first start, multiple marker pairs, a missing end marker, adjacent document text, and a marker at end of file. The reference marker expressions use literal spaces and its reconstruction does not always ensure a blank line after the end marker; use the issue's stronger requirements as the acceptance criteria.\\n- An existing TOC title can itself be a heading: exclude the entire selected region before collection. With a missing end marker, decide insertion boundaries carefully so ordinary headings following the start remain available.\\n- Ignore handling uses placeholders and restores them after the callback. Verify that markers and headings in ignored blocks do not cause false positives, and that direct utility calls do not accidentally bypass the intended protection.\\n- Check no headings, all headings excluded, a title without entries, level boundaries, skipped levels, zero indentation, and sequential numbering across different nesting levels.\\n- Test links with aliases, images, inline formatting, trailing hashes, explicit IDs, repeated normalized headings, and collisions between naturally suffixed names and deduplicated names. Keep display text and anchor normalization independent.\\n- Invalid slash-delimited regex patterns should not crash the entire rule; the reference falls back to treating them as literals. Verify textarea conversion and defaults for both framework-supplied and direct options.\\n- This is guidance only: the repository and reference patch must remain unchanged here. The original issue's branch and commit request is for implementation work, not this read-only review stage.\\n\"}"}]}

{"content":"","tool_calls":[{"name":"Write","arguments":"{\"file_path\":\"/tmp/hint_output.md\",\"content\":\"# CREATE TABLE guidance\\n\\n## Problem Essence\\n\\nThe current main lexer routes top-level `create` statements to the unsupported-DDL ruleset, which treats their contents as formatting-disabled data rather than identifying a table body and its items. Even after recognizing a body, the generic splitter and merger do not know which boundaries must remain separate or which nested expressions must stay together, and there is no public DDL inspection module.\\n\\n## Key Files and Locations\\n\\n- `src/sqlfmt/rules/__init__.py`: `MAIN` selects specialized rules before `unsupported_ddl`; this is the entry point for recognizing supported table headers and post-body clauses.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/rules/ddl.py` (new): a context-specific body ruleset distinguishes table and inline constraints while retaining core SQL lexing.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/actions.py`: rule actions emit nodes and manage nested rulesets; body closure and post-body termination need to return control correctly.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/tokens.py`: token categories determine bracket behavior, spacing, keyword normalization, and query boundaries.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/node_manager.py`: creates nodes, computes bracket stacks and whitespace, checks matching brackets, and normalizes token values.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/node.py`: node predicates expose token kinds and bracket context to later passes.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/line.py`: line depth and predicates provide structural information for formatting decisions.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/splitter.py`: splits at generic syntax boundaries; DDL item boundaries must be recognized without confusing nested commas for body separators.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/merger.py`: merges split segments when they fit; it needs to preserve DDL structural boundaries while allowing individual expressions to recombine.\\n- `src/sqlfmt/ddl.py` (new): provides the requested value objects and extracts a table description from parsed lines.\\n\\nFor the data flow, also follow `api.format_string` through `Analyzer.parse_query` and `QueryFormatter.format`: parsing precedes splitting, Jinja handling, and merging. `rules/core.py` supplies common bracket, comma, and name rules; `rules/unsupported.py` explains existing pass-through behavior.\\n\\n## Solution Approach\\n\\nModel a supported CREATE TABLE column-list as a distinct bracket scope, so all downstream stages can distinguish the body from nested type parameters, constraint expressions, and later clauses. Identify body items using their position and relative depth, rather than relying on the input already having one item per line. Let existing formatting machinery handle ordinary expressions where possible, but preserve the required header, item, closer, clause, and semicolon boundaries across both splitting and merging.\\n\\nBuild the inspection API on the parsed nodes rather than formatted line text. It should traverse items in source order, distinguish column definitions from table constraints, and reconstruct type expressions using original token spacing while normalizing the required words.\\n\\n## Implementation Directions\\n\\n1. Trace `MAIN` rule priority and the existing nested-ruleset actions. Recognize only supported table headers before the generic unsupported rule, including `IF NOT EXISTS`, and preserve the existing route for out-of-scope statements. Ensure closing the outer body, not a nested parenthesis, changes the active ruleset; handle post-body clauses and the statement terminator without leaking rules into the next statement.\\n2. Connect the new structural token kinds to bracket opening and matching in `TokenType` and `NodeManager`. Check how `open_brackets` is inherited from the previous node and popped on a closer; the header's opener needs to participate consistently in indentation and mismatch checks. Normalize keywords and types without unintentionally changing quoted identifiers.\\n3. Expose body membership and relative depth through node/line helpers as needed. Use these to distinguish the body-level comma from commas inside type arguments, functions, and constraints. Review `NodeManager.whitespace` for the difference between name-followed parentheses and keyword-followed parentheses, especially `CHECK` and table constraints.\\n4. Inspect both `LineSplitter.maybe_split` and `LineMerger.create_merged_line`: a split alone is insufficient because the merger can undo it. Preserve one body item per line and isolate the header and body closer, but permit nested portions of an individual item and each post-body argument list to remain on one line. Account for the specified line-length exceptions rather than disabling length checks globally.\\n5. In the new public module, implement value-based equality on public fields, defaults, counts, filtered column properties, and the constraint marker in column string conversion. Walk nodes across line boundaries until the outer body ends; recognize table-level `CHECK` and named constraints as well as key constraints. For each column, stop the type at the first specified inline constraint at body depth, and reconstruct its type using source token prefixes rather than joining token values with arbitrary spaces.\\n6. Add focused tests using the existing analyzer, splitter, merger, and formatter test patterns. Exercise both raw parsed lines and formatted/reparsed lines, plus end-to-end output and idempotence. Run the relevant existing tests as regression coverage.\\n\\n## Pitfalls and Edge Cases\\n\\n- Test flat and multiline source, nested `array`/`struct` types, parameterized types with internal commas, function calls, `REFERENCES`, and `CHECK` expressions. A nested comma or closing parenthesis must never end the outer item or body.\\n- Test bare and named table constraints alongside inline constraints, including multiple constraints on a column; do not classify a constraint argument or name as another column. The module contract's inline terminators and original inter-token spacing matter independently of formatted output.\\n- Check `CHECK (` and table-constraint keyword spacing separately from `name(...)`, and ensure each body separator is retained with no final trailing comma. Verify quoted and qualified identifiers and case-sensitive dialect behavior.\\n- Test multiple post-body clauses and a following statement, with and without a semicolon where valid, to catch ruleset and depth leakage. `OPTIONS` recognition should be scoped so ordinary SQL identifiers are unaffected.\\n- Long definitions and post-body clauses may exceed the limit only when their minimal single-line forms already do; other lines still need to respect it. Comments, formatting-disabled regions, and existing non-DDL formatting deserve regression tests.\\n- `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` and `CREATE TABLE ... LIKE ...` must pass through unchanged. The reference patch is a design aid, not proof that every stated boundary is covered: explicitly test the full issue contract, including unsupported variants and raw parsed representations.\\n\\nThe original issue asks for a branch and commit, but this guidance stage operates on a read-only repository and does not make repository changes.\\n\"}"}]}

{"content":"","tool_calls":[{"name":"Write","arguments":"{\"file_path\":\"/tmp/hint_output.md\",\"content\":\"# Grid layout implementation guide\\n\\n## Problem Essence\\n\\nThe current style API only permits `flex` and `none`, and its Yoga display mapping treats anything other than `flex` as hidden. The rendering pipeline relies on Yoga's computed flex layout, but there is no grid track sizing or placement pass, so exposing a new string alone cannot produce a grid.\\n\\n## Key Files and Locations\\n\\n- `src/styles.ts` — `Styles` defines the public style properties used by `<Box>`, while `applyDisplayStyles` maps display values to Yoga. The existing gap properties and `applyGapStyles` are also here. The reference changes this file to expose grid templates and placement and to keep grid nodes visible to Yoga.\\n- `src/grid-layout.ts` — a new file in the reference patch, not present in the inspected initial implementation. It parses tracks and placement, measures content, resolves track sizes, assigns children to cells, and applies the resulting geometry to Yoga nodes.\\n- `src/renderer.ts` — creates the output buffer from computed Yoga dimensions and invokes the output traversal. The reference adds the grid pass before ordinary rendering and considers descendant extents when determining output height.\\n\\nOther useful context: `src/components/Box.tsx` derives its props from `Styles` and forwards them as style; `src/reconciler.ts` stores the full style on DOM nodes and applies style changes to Yoga. `src/dom.ts` describes the element/text tree and text measurement, and `src/render-node-to-output.ts` reads computed positions relative to parents. `src/ink.tsx` and `src/render-to-string.ts` run the initial Yoga calculation. `test/display.tsx` shows the existing render-test pattern.\\n\\n## Solution Approach\\n\\nTreat grid as a layout mode layered on top of Yoga rather than as a Yoga display constant. Preserve the grid style on the DOM element, use Yoga to obtain the container's computed dimensions, then resolve grid tracks and child cell geometry before the normal output traversal consumes those positions. Only `none` should map to Yoga's hidden display; ordinary flex behavior must remain intact.\\n\\nSeparate the work conceptually into parsing, placement, track sizing, and geometry application. Placement must be known before content-dependent tracks can be measured; resolved track sizes and gaps then determine each child's position and span size. Account for the container's content box and for automatic height when the rows determine how tall the grid needs to be.\\n\\n## Implementation Directions\\n\\n1. Extend the public style type with `grid` and the two template and two placement properties. Follow the existing `Box` → reconciler → DOM style flow to verify that grid-specific values remain available to the layout pass. Adjust the Yoga display mapping so grid is not hidden.\\n2. In a dedicated grid layout module, represent fixed, fractional, auto, and minmax tracks explicitly. Tokenize templates at whitespace outside parentheses, so spaces inside `minmax(…, …)` do not split a track. Parse placement into zero-based starts and spans, remembering that the public line indices are one-based and an end line is exclusive.\\n3. Reserve explicitly placed cells before placing remaining children in row-major order. Track occupied cells across spans and create implicit auto rows as needed, including when the row template is omitted. Consider how a child with only one axis specified should be handled.\\n4. For each axis, subtract border, padding, and inter-track gaps from available space. Resolve fixed and content-sized tracks and all minmax minimums before distributing nonnegative remaining space by fractional weights. A minmax track with an `fr` maximum starts at its minimum and receives its proportional share of that remainder. Decide and test the behavior of fixed minmax maxima as well.\\n5. Use the resolved tracks to calculate each cell's offset and size, including internal gaps for spans. The reference applies absolute positions and dimensions to child Yoga nodes and recalculates layout; inspect the existing positioning and sizing conventions carefully before doing so. For an unspecified grid height, derive a height from rows, gaps, padding, and borders.\\n6. Integrate the pass after the initial Yoga calculation and before rendering. Trace nested grids and output-buffer height, including the separate static and screen-reader paths, so that geometry is available where needed and content is not clipped simply because the original root height was too small.\\n7. Add focused render and type-level tests using existing test conventions. Verify both the new behavior and unchanged `flex`/`none` behavior.\\n\\n## Pitfalls and Edge Cases\\n\\n- Test mixed fixed, `auto`, `fr`, and `minmax` tracks, including whitespace within `minmax`, unequal fractional weights, no remaining space, and rounding to terminal cells. Do not allocate the same remaining space multiple times to fixed-maximum tracks.\\n- Test automatic rows, explicit positions beyond initial rows, spans and their included gaps, mixed explicit and automatic children, and the exclusive end line. Guard empty or malformed templates and invalid indices against division by zero or invalid coordinates; define behavior rather than relying on accidental parsing.\\n- `columnGap` and `rowGap` should override the shorthand independently, including explicit zero values. Account for padding and border on both axes and distinguish the content box from the outer dimensions.\\n- Auto measurement should reflect terminal display width and multiline content; `measureText` uses terminal-aware width, while `dom.ts` also handles wrapping. Spanning items, wrapping, nested boxes, and explicit child sizes deserve targeted tests rather than assuming raw text measurements cover them.\\n- Yoga mutations persist across renders. Check resizing, changed templates and children, and switching grid back to flex or none; restore or recompute grid-assigned positioning and dimensions as appropriate. Also check nested grids, hidden children, clipping, static output, layout listeners, and screen-reader behavior.\\n- The reference is a useful design example, not proof that every edge case is correct: in particular, inspect how it handles partial placement, sizing multiple fixed-maximum minmax tracks, and nested or dynamically updated layouts. The issue does not require `repeat()`, named lines, or configurable auto-flow.\\n\\nThe original issue asks for a branch and commit, but this guidance stage is read-only and does not modify the repository; implementation and its commit are for the student.\\n\"}"}]}

{"content":"","tool_calls":[{"name":"Write","arguments":"{\"file_path\":\"/tmp/hint_output.md\",\"content\":\"# Feature Schema Persistence: Initial Guidance\\n\\n## Problem Essence\\n\\n`Igel._process_data` currently converts the columns present in each incoming dataset directly to arrays, after preprocessing and, for supervised training, removing targets. It neither records which raw features were used nor aligns later inputs to that order, so additional, missing, or reordered columns can change model inputs; export also assumes a fixed width of four.\\n\\n## Key Files and Locations\\n\\n- **`igel/constants.py`**: Defines artifact names such as `model_file` and `description_file`; it is the natural location for the schema artifact name.\\n- **`igel/configs.py`**: Defines results paths and default and available dataset properties. Feature selection options and the schema path need to be represented consistently here.\\n- **`igel/preprocessing.py`**: Contains data-reading and preprocessing helpers. This is a suitable place for fitting and applying a raw-feature schema, independent of the estimator.\\n- **`igel/igel.py`**: `__init__` resolves paths and loads training metadata; `_process_data` prepares all model inputs; `fit` saves the model and description; `evaluate`, `_get_predictions`, and `export` consume artifacts. These are the integration points for the schema lifecycle.\\n- **`igel/servers/fastapi_server.py`**: `/predict` converts the request to a temporary CSV and invokes `Igel`; it must translate schema validation errors into HTTP 400 responses and clean up the temporary file.\\n\\n## Solution Approach\\n\\nTreat the raw feature schema as a fitted artifact, separate from model preprocessing. During fit, determine the ordered surviving raw columns and duplicate aliases before encoding, imputation, scaling, or conversion to NumPy; persist that artifact alongside the model and summarize it in `description.json`. At evaluation and prediction time, load it and construct an ordered frame with the same canonical names before any model call.\\n\\nKeep targets outside feature selection but retain them for supervised fit and evaluation. Clustering has no target, yet needs the same fitted-schema and inference alignment rules. Export should obtain the estimator's input width from training description metadata rather than its current hard-coded value; distinguish raw selected width from any width changed by preprocessing.\\n\\n## Implementation Directions\\n\\n1. {"content":"# Auto TOC implementation guide

The complete guide was written to `/tmp/hint_output.md`.

## Problem Essence

The current repository has no Auto TOC rule or TOC-generation utility, so opting in with a marker cannot produce or update a contents list. The existing heading regex and rule framework provide useful pieces, but they do not themselves identify a TOC region, construct anchors, or prevent headings in ignored blocks from being collected.

## Key Files and Locations

- `src/rules/auto-toc.ts` (new): define and default-export the registered content rule, its option defaults, settings controls, examples, and the call into the TOC utility. Declare code, math, and YAML ignore types in the rule metadata.
- `src/utils/toc.ts` (new): isolate marker handling, heading extraction, text normalization, exclusions, anchor deduplication, and list generation from the UI-facing rule.
- `src/rules-runner.ts`: import the new rule so its registration decorator executes and the normal rule loop can discover it. The reference patch adds an import rather than a special execution path.
- `src/lang/locale/en.ts`: add the rule and option name/description keys and dropdown enum labels used by the builders.
- `src/rules/rule-builder.ts`: inspect `NumberOptionBuilder` and its generic key constraint. The reference changes its value type from `Number` to `any` to accommodate the new numeric options; consider the wider type-safety impact when making the change.

Supporting code worth studying: `src/utils/regex.ts` defines `allHeadersRegex` and its capture groups; `src/utils/ignore-types.ts` implements placeholder-based ignore handling; `src/rules/remove-trailing-punctuation-in-heading.ts` and `src/rules/ordered-list-style.ts` show existing rule patterns.

## Solution Approach

Connect a conventional `RuleBuilder` rule to a focused utility. The framework constructs options and registers the rule, while the utility finds the first opt-in marker, collects eligible headings outside the selected TOC region, and replaces or inserts the generated content. Preserve the rest of the document and return it unchanged when there is no start marker.

Separate the heading's displayed text from its anchor: resolve links and remove embeds and formatting when creating the anchor, but only strip displayed formatting when the corresponding option requests it. Apply exclusions before rendering, maintain a document-order counter for duplicate bases, and render indentation and list markers from the options.

## Implementation Directions

1. Follow a nearby registered rule to implement the class, `OptionsClass`, examples, and option builders. Provide the defaults in the issue; ensure dropdown values have matching English locale keys. Trace how `buildRuleOptions` converts configuration keys into properties, including the newline-separated textarea. Numeric settings are presented through a text option, so account for conversion at the rule boundary.
2. In the utility, locate markers case-insensitively with whitespace tolerance. Match the first end marker *after* the first start, and distinguish an existing region from a missing end marker. Rebuild the region with the requested blank-line boundaries, preserving surrounding content and ensuring a second run is stable.
3. Inspect `allHeadersRegex`: its second capture is the hash sequence and its fourth is the heading text; it also has a separate optional closing-hash capture. Filter heading levels to the configured range and exclude positions in the selected TOC region. Use the rule's ignore mechanism for YAML, code, and math, and verify the actual rule execution path as well as direct calls to the utility.
4. Normalize heading text in a deliberate order: remove wiki and Markdown image embeds before resolving ordinary links to display text, remove formatting and trailing heading hashes, then lowercase, replace whitespace, filter characters, collapse hyphens, and trim them. Handle a trailing explicit ID separately when enabled. Track repeated anchor bases while processing headings in order.
5. Compare exclusions case-insensitively, distinguishing slash-delimited regular expressions from literal entries. Render the optional title and each surviving heading with the requested marker, indentation relative to `minLevel`, and either constant or globally incrementing ordered numbers.
6. Add focused tests using the repository's existing rule-test conventions. Cover the rule through its framework entry point as well as any utility-level behavior; check expected output and idempotence rather than only whether an entry exists.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- Test no marker, mixed case and tabs in markers, an end marker before the first start, multiple marker pairs, a missing end marker, adjacent document text, and a marker at end of file. The reference marker expressions use literal spaces and its reconstruction does not always ensure a blank line after the end marker; use the issue's stronger requirements as the acceptance criteria.
- An existing TOC title can itself be a heading: exclude the entire selected region before collection. With a missing end marker, decide insertion boundaries carefully so ordinary headings following the start remain available.
- Ignore handling uses placeholders and restores them after the callback. Verify that markers and headings in ignored blocks do not cause false positives, and that direct utility calls do not accidentally bypass the intended protection.
- Check no headings, all headings excluded, a title without entries, level boundaries, skipped levels, zero indentation, and sequential numbering across different nesting levels.
- Test links with aliases, images, inline formatting, trailing hashes, explicit IDs, repeated normalized headings, and collisions between naturally suffixed names and deduplicated names. Keep display text and anchor normalization independent.
- Invalid slash-delimited regex patterns should not crash the entire rule; the reference falls back to treating them as literals. Verify textarea conversion and defaults for both framework-supplied and direct options.
- This is guidance only: the repository and reference patch must remain unchanged here. The original issue's branch and commit request is for implementation work, not this read-only review stage.","tool_calls":[]}

{"content":"# CREATE TABLE guidance

The complete guide was written to `/tmp/hint_output.md`.

## Problem Essence

The current main lexer routes top-level `create` statements to the unsupported-DDL ruleset, which treats their contents as formatting-disabled data rather than identifying a table body and its items. Even after recognizing a body, the generic splitter and merger do not know which boundaries must remain separate or which nested expressions must stay together, and there is no public DDL inspection module.

## Key Files and Locations

- `src/sqlfmt/rules/__init__.py`: `MAIN` selects specialized rules before `unsupported_ddl`; this is the entry point for recognizing supported table headers and post-body clauses.
- `src/sqlfmt/rules/ddl.py` (new): a context-specific body ruleset distinguishes table and inline constraints while retaining core SQL lexing.
- `src/sqlfmt/actions.py`: rule actions emit nodes and manage nested rulesets; body closure and post-body termination need to return control correctly.
- `src/sqlfmt/tokens.py`: token categories determine bracket behavior, spacing, keyword normalization, and query boundaries.
- `src/sqlfmt/node_manager.py`: creates nodes, computes bracket stacks and whitespace, checks matching brackets, and normalizes token values.
- `src/sqlfmt/node.py`: node predicates expose token kinds and bracket context to later passes.
- `src/sqlfmt/line.py`: line depth and predicates provide structural information for formatting decisions.
- `src/sqlfmt/splitter.py`: splits at generic syntax boundaries; DDL item boundaries must be recognized without confusing nested commas for body separators.
- `src/sqlfmt/merger.py`: merges split segments when they fit; it needs to preserve DDL structural boundaries while allowing individual expressions to recombine.
- `src/sqlfmt/ddl.py` (new): provides the requested value objects and extracts a table description from parsed lines.

For the data flow, also follow `api.format_string` through `Analyzer.parse_query` and `QueryFormatter.format`: parsing precedes splitting, Jinja handling, and merging. `rules/core.py` supplies common bracket, comma, and name rules; `rules/unsupported.py` explains existing pass-through behavior.

## Solution Approach

Model a supported CREATE TABLE column-list as a distinct bracket scope, so all downstream stages can distinguish the body from nested type parameters, constraint expressions, and later clauses. Identify body items using their position and relative depth, rather than relying on the input already having one item per line. Let existing formatting machinery handle ordinary expressions where possible, but preserve the required header, item, closer, clause, and semicolon boundaries across both splitting and merging.

Build the inspection API on the parsed nodes rather than formatted line text. It should traverse items in source order, distinguish column definitions from table constraints, and reconstruct type expressions using original token spacing while normalizing the required words.

## Implementation Directions

1. Trace `MAIN` rule priority and the existing nested-ruleset actions. Recognize only supported table headers before the generic unsupported rule, including `IF NOT EXISTS`, and preserve the existing route for out-of-scope statements. Ensure closing the outer body, not a nested parenthesis, changes the active ruleset; handle post-body clauses and the statement terminator without leaking rules into the next statement.
2. Connect the new structural token kinds to bracket opening and matching in `TokenType` and `NodeManager`. Check how `open_brackets` is inherited from the previous node and popped on a closer; the header's opener needs to participate consistently in indentation and mismatch checks. Normalize keywords and types without unintentionally changing quoted identifiers.
3. Expose body membership and relative depth through node/line helpers as needed. Use these to distinguish the body-level comma from commas inside type arguments, functions, and constraints. Review `NodeManager.whitespace` for the difference between name-followed parentheses and keyword-followed parentheses, especially `CHECK` and table constraints.
4. Inspect both `LineSplitter.maybe_split` and `LineMerger.create_merged_line`: a split alone is insufficient because the merger can undo it. Preserve one body item per line and isolate the header and body closer, but permit nested portions of an individual item and each post-body argument list to remain on one line. Account for the specified line-length exceptions rather than disabling length checks globally.
5. In the new public module, implement value-based equality on public fields, defaults, counts, filtered column properties, and the constraint marker in column string conversion. Walk nodes across line boundaries until the outer body ends; recognize table-level `CHECK` and named constraints as well as key constraints. For each column, stop the type at the first specified inline constraint at body depth, and reconstruct its type using source token prefixes rather than joining token values with arbitrary spaces.
6. Add focused tests using the existing analyzer, splitter, merger, and formatter test patterns. Exercise both raw parsed lines and formatted/reparsed lines, plus end-to-end output and idempotence. Run the relevant existing tests as regression coverage.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- Test flat and multiline source, nested `array`/`struct` types, parameterized types with internal commas, function calls, `REFERENCES`, and `CHECK` expressions. A nested comma or closing parenthesis must never end the outer item or body.
- Test bare and named table constraints alongside inline constraints, including multiple constraints on a column; do not classify a constraint argument or name as another column. The module contract's inline terminators and original inter-token spacing matter independently of formatted output.
- Check `CHECK (` and table-constraint keyword spacing separately from `name(...)`, and ensure each body separator is retained with no final trailing comma. Verify quoted and qualified identifiers and case-sensitive dialect behavior.
- Test multiple post-body clauses and a following statement, with and without a semicolon where valid, to catch ruleset and depth leakage. `OPTIONS` recognition should be scoped so ordinary SQL identifiers are unaffected.
- Long definitions and post-body clauses may exceed the limit only when their minimal single-line forms already do; other lines still need to respect it. Comments, formatting-disabled regions, and existing non-DDL formatting deserve regression tests.
- `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` and `CREATE TABLE ... LIKE ...` must pass through unchanged. The reference patch is a design aid, not proof that every stated boundary is covered: explicitly test the full issue contract, including unsupported variants and raw parsed representations.

The original issue asks for a branch and commit, but this guidance stage operates on a read-only repository and does not make repository changes.","tool_calls":[]}

{"content":"# Grid layout implementation guide

The guide was written to `/tmp/hint_output.md`.

## Problem Essence

The current style API only permits `flex` and `none`, and its Yoga display mapping treats anything other than `flex` as hidden. The rendering pipeline relies on Yoga's computed flex layout, but there is no grid track sizing or placement pass, so exposing a new string alone cannot produce a grid.

## Key Files and Locations

- `src/styles.ts` — `Styles` defines the public style properties used by `<Box>`, while `applyDisplayStyles` maps display values to Yoga. The existing gap properties and `applyGapStyles` are also here. The reference changes this file to expose grid templates and placement and to keep grid nodes visible to Yoga.
- `src/grid-layout.ts` — a new file in the reference patch, not present in the inspected initial implementation. It parses tracks and placement, measures content, resolves track sizes, assigns children to cells, and applies the resulting geometry to Yoga nodes.
- `src/renderer.ts` — creates the output buffer from computed Yoga dimensions and invokes the output traversal. The reference adds the grid pass before ordinary rendering and considers descendant extents when determining output height.

Other useful context: `src/components/Box.tsx` derives its props from `Styles` and forwards them as style; `src/reconciler.ts` stores the full style on DOM nodes and applies style changes to Yoga. `src/dom.ts` describes the element/text tree and text measurement, and `src/render-node-to-output.ts` reads computed positions relative to parents. `src/ink.tsx` and `src/render-to-string.ts` run the initial Yoga calculation. `test/display.tsx` shows the existing render-test pattern.

## Solution Approach

Treat grid as a layout mode layered on top of Yoga rather than as a Yoga display constant. Preserve the grid style on the DOM element, use Yoga to obtain the container's computed dimensions, then resolve grid tracks and child cell geometry before the normal output traversal consumes those positions. Only `none` should map to Yoga's hidden display; ordinary flex behavior must remain intact.

Separate the work conceptually into parsing, placement, track sizing, and geometry application. Placement must be known before content-dependent tracks can be measured; resolved track sizes and gaps then determine each child's position and span size. Account for the container's content box and for automatic height when the rows determine how tall the grid needs to be.

## Implementation Directions

1. Extend the public style type with `grid` and the two template and two placement properties. Follow the existing `Box` → reconciler → DOM style flow to verify that grid-specific values remain available to the layout pass. Adjust the Yoga display mapping so grid is not hidden.
2. In a dedicated grid layout module, represent fixed, fractional, auto, and minmax tracks explicitly. Tokenize templates at whitespace outside parentheses, so spaces inside `minmax(…, …)` do not split a track. Parse placement into zero-based starts and spans, remembering that the public line indices are one-based and an end line is exclusive.
3. Reserve explicitly placed cells before placing remaining children in row-major order. Track occupied cells across spans and create implicit auto rows as needed, including when the row template is omitted. Consider how a child with only one axis specified should be handled.
4. For each axis, subtract border, padding, and inter-track gaps from available space. Resolve fixed and content-sized tracks and all minmax minimums before distributing nonnegative remaining space by fractional weights. A minmax track with an `fr` maximum starts at its minimum and receives its proportional share of that remainder. Decide and test the behavior of fixed minmax maxima as well.
5. Use the resolved tracks to calculate each cell's offset and size, including internal gaps for spans. The reference applies absolute positions and dimensions to child Yoga nodes and recalculates layout; inspect the existing positioning and sizing conventions carefully before doing so. For an unspecified grid height, derive a height from rows, gaps, padding, and borders.
6. Integrate the pass after the initial Yoga calculation and before rendering. Trace nested grids and output-buffer height, including the separate static and screen-reader paths, so that geometry is available where needed and content is not clipped simply because the original root height was too small.
7. Add focused render and type-level tests using existing test conventions. Verify both the new behavior and unchanged `flex`/`none` behavior.

## Pitfalls and Edge Cases

- Test mixed fixed, `auto`, `fr`, and `minmax` tracks, including whitespace within `minmax`, unequal fractional weights, no remaining space, and rounding to terminal cells. Do not allocate the same remaining space multiple times to fixed-maximum tracks.
- Test automatic rows, explicit positions beyond initial rows, spans and their included gaps, mixed explicit and automatic children, and the exclusive end line. Guard empty or malformed templates and invalid indices against division by zero or invalid coordinates; define behavior rather than relying on accidental parsing.
- `columnGap` and `rowGap` should override the shorthand independently, including explicit zero values. Account for padding and border on both axes and distinguish the content box from the outer dimensions.
- Auto measurement should reflect terminal display width and multiline content; `measureText` uses terminal-aware width, while `dom.ts` also handles wrapping. Spanning items, wrapping, nested boxes, and explicit child sizes deserve targeted tests rather than assuming raw text measurements cover them.
- Yoga mutations persist across renders. Check resizing, changed templates and children, and switching grid back to flex or none; restore or recompute grid-assigned positioning and dimensions as appropriate. Also check nested grids, hidden children, clipping, static output, layout listeners, and screen-reader behavior.
- The reference is a useful design example, not proof that every edge case is correct: in particular, inspect how it handles partial placement, sizing multiple fixed-maximum minmax tracks, and nested or dynamically updated layouts. The issue does not require `repeat()`, named lines, or configurable auto-flow.

The original issue asks for a branch and commit, but this guidance stage is read-only and does not modify the repository; implementation and its commit are for the student.","tool_calls":[]}
